finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::ssrf / internal network probing: datasource host and port are fully user-controlled with no allowlist, and connection errors are returned to the caller as an oracle
evidence: The supplied datasource.service.ts confirms every factual element of the claim: `create`/`update` persist `dto.host`/`dto.port` with no allowlist or private-range check (the DTO in datasource.dto.ts only enforces string length 1-253 and port 1-65535), `createClient` (the `new Client({ host: ds.host, port: ds.port, ... connectionTimeoutMillis: 10_000 })` block at the end of the file, the line the diff touches to add `types`) dials that address directly, and `testConnection` returns `{ success: false, error: (error as Error).message }` verbatim to the caller — with `executeQuery` similarly surfacing `pgError.message` in a BadRequestException. So an authenticated workspace member can use these endpoints as an internal host/port existence oracle, distinguishing ECONNREFUSED / timeout / auth-failure / non-Postgres-service responses; the controller only checks workspace membership, never destination. Two caveats that temper but do not falsify it: this behavior is entirely pre-existing (the diff only adds a type-parser option to the same constructor call), and it is the inherent design of a user-configured DB connector, so the practical severity depends on network egress controls I cannot inspect; the trust-auth read-access escalation is explicitly unconfirmed by the reviewer as well.
